summary: Sam Rutherford's Engadget review praises Super Mario Bros. Wonder as a polished, inventive 2D Mario that stays fresh after nearly 40 years. The key innovation is the Wonder Flower, which rewrites the rules of a level, supported by new badges, varied level types, a lived-in Flower Kingdom and better difficulty pacing. He has only minor complaints and compares the game favorably to Super Mario World.
one_line: Engadget's review hails Super Mario Bros. Wonder as a dazzling, inventive 2D Mario whose Wonder Flowers and polish keep the franchise fresh.
key_facts: Super Mario Bros. Wonder is set in the Flower Kingdom, where Bowser steals a Wonder Flower and merges with Prince Florian's castle to create a floating mecha fortress.
Daisy is a playable character for the first time, and Mario has a new voice actor for the first time.
Players collect Wonder Seeds, this game's version of stars and shines.
The game features six main worlds, each with a distinctive theme, including reimagined haunted houses, pirate ships and underwater stages.
Badges are earned by completing specific levels; they grant abilities like farther jumps or floating, extra coins, and protection such as being saved from falling into lava or poison.
Rutherford says the badge system feels inspired by recent roguelikes such as Hades and adds customizability and replayability.

Wonder Flowers are hidden in almost every stage and transport players to an alternate dimension with rewritten rules, such as raining Super Stars, becoming a giant slime, a top-down 2D maze, or a shooting gallery.
In Nintendo's Ask the Developer, the team reportedly had a wall of sticky notes with over 2,000 ideas.
Level types include classic flag stages, races, badge challenges, puzzle levels, KO Arenas (choose Fire Flower, Elephant Suit, Bubble Mushroom or Drill Hat), and Break Time levels of 30 seconds.
Difficulty ratings and hidden paths let players reach 5-star levels long before finishing the game, fixing a pacing complaint about earlier 2D Marios.
Minor complaints: tedious mummy enemies, an Elephant Suit possibly overpowered versus the Drill Hat, wanting more 5-star and rhythm levels, and no penguins from the movie in ice levels.
Rutherford says it may be the best Mario has looked, including versus 3D titles like Odyssey, and likens Wonder to his favorite 2D Mario, Super Mario World.
It took more than 10 years for Nintendo to make a proper sequel to its last mainline 2D platformer.
